title: ResultSafe Core architecture decisions
summary: Binding architecture decisions reached during the independent audit and ResultSafe platform design session.

items.title: Independent ResultSafe canon
items.decision: ResultSafe owns an independent canonical contract corpus and integrates with AASDVGS only through separately governed admission.
items.rationale: This preserves ResultSafe language neutrality and avoids claiming authority from a staged external kernel candidate.
consequences: External publication IDs are not minted locally

items.title: Neutral algebra with projections
items.decision: Canonical Result uses SUCCESS and FAILURE semantics while TypeScript, Python, and AASDVGS define distinct strict representations.
items.rationale: Wire field names and runtime classes are language or integration choices rather than universal algebra.

items.title: Standards-first identifiers
items.decision: Internal entity IDs use UUIDv7, public handles use UUIDv4 only when required, and canonical references use absolute URIs.
items.rationale: RFC-defined formats prevent proprietary identity encodings and preserve interoperability.
consequences: UUIDv7 never establishes authority or chronology

items.title: JSON canonical authority
items.decision: Strict canonical JSON and JSON Schema are authoritative; Markdown, source code, SQLite, and generated documentation are projections or evidence.
items.rationale: Reviewable deterministic text prevents binary authority and bidirectional synchronization conflicts.

items.title: Separate package families
items.decision: Contracts, language runtimes, storage projections, projection compilers, and integration adapters use separate package families.
items.rationale: Separate ownership and release cadence prevent a runtime implementation from becoming platform authority.
consequences: SQLite profile is independent from compiler language
Each family has independent integrity evidence

items.title: Database is a storage projection
items.decision: Database representations are platform storage projections and are not attached to TypeScript, Python, or another language runtime.
items.rationale: A compiler implementation language must not redefine projection semantics or ownership.

items.title: SQLite derived release artifact
items.decision: SQLite is a vendor profile over the relational projection and generated databases are versioned release artifacts, never Git authority.
items.rationale: Binary databases are unsuitable for canonical review but valuable as verified query read models.

items.title: Targeted TypeScript stabilization
items.decision: Stabilize the complete Result package boundary and directly duplicated dependencies without rewriting unrelated TypeScript platform modules.
items.rationale: The smallest correct boundary is the Result family plus its concrete shared type and Option interoperability obligations.
consequences: Unrelated FP modules require separate audits

items.title: Schema-driven refiners
items.decision: Refiners use explicit runtime validation evidence, own-field rules, required payload presence, and typed validator output rather than erased generics.
items.rationale: A type guard cannot safely assert information unavailable at runtime.
consequences: Legacy never sentinel is projection-only deprecated input

items.title: Immutable matcher builder
items.decision: Both matchers use one immutable accumulated handler state and strict run availability is based on an empty remaining-variant set.
items.rationale: The current nested closures lose handlers and the conditional type tests only membership rather than exhaustiveness.

items.title: Separate npm contracts and runtime
items.decision: Publish canonical contract artifacts and the TypeScript runtime as separate npm packages linked by release reference and digest.
items.rationale: Npm is a distribution channel and runtime users should not acquire registry tooling or database dependencies.
consequences: Runtime metadata pins contract release digest

items.title: Governed AASDVGS admission
items.decision: ResultSafe prepares an admission dossier but performs no AASDVGS authority mutation without separately approved governed work.
items.rationale: The active AASDVGS work scope and staged kernel candidate do not authorize a new ResultSafe package family.

items.title: Defer security and long-running tests
items.decision: Security hardening and long-running tests are deferred and MUST NOT run without an explicit owner command.
items.rationale: The owner standing decision remains mandatory while normal fast correctness and integrity checks remain permitted.
consequences: NOT_EXECUTED is never promoted to PASS

items.title: Adopt optional structured Failure
items.decision: Provide Failure as an explicit portable payload with required schema_version and absolute-URI code while Result<T,E>, Err<E>, and FailureData<E> remain generic.
items.rationale: Comparative evidence favors generic error channels, while interoperability and security require an available strict structure at selected boundaries.
consequences: Existing arbitrary E values remain valid
Strict integration profiles may require Failure

items.title: Optional Cause and Exit models
items.decision: Adopt separate Cause and Exit canonical models without changing generic Result, Err, or the neutral Result operation surface.
items.rationale: The audit winner preserves complete failure topology while retaining every previously valid generic Result error and success value.
consequences: Binary grouping and order are normative

items.title: Semantic Effect compatibility only
items.decision: Describe Effect compatibility as explicit semantic mappings and never as runtime, wire-format, identity, or dependency compatibility.
items.rationale: Effect concepts provide useful semantic correspondence but external runtime identities and representations are not portable ResultSafe values.
consequences: TypeScript and Python projections are independently qualified
No Effect runtime dependency enters core

items.title: Root plus derived direct subpaths
items.decision: Expose every intended TypeScript core public module through the root and a stable direct subpath whose artifact targets follow one normative source-to-artifact derivation rule.
items.rationale: A single derivation prevents hand-maintained dist path drift while direct imports preserve modular consumption and tree-shaking.
consequences: The public module registry is authoritative for intended module membership
UMD remains a root-only browser bundle
Packed-artifact proof is mandatory before a conformance claim
Result remains exactly 23 neutral operations and 88 matrix cells

items.title: Explicit codecs in a separate package
items.decision: Implement portable Cause and Exit JSON codecs only in @resultsafe/core-fp-codec-json and keep codec operations absent from the core package dependency graph.
items.rationale: Serialization policy is boundary-specific and must not become an implicit representation or mandatory runtime cost for generic Result consumers.
consequences: Valid and malformed vectors are governed
Core retains zero dependency on the codec package

items.title: Effect runtime in a separate adapter
items.decision: Make @resultsafe/adapter-core-fp-effect the sole mapping authority for executable Effect interoperability, with Effect 3.22.1 as the exact supported peer version.
items.rationale: A separate package preserves the zero-dependency core while allowing executable version-specific mappings without claiming representation identity.
consequences: The adapter owns executable mapping evidence
Exact effect@3.22.1 is QUALIFIED_LOCAL_SNAPSHOT by PASS_LOCAL_ATOMIC evidence and is not release-approved
